target_customer: Software companies selling B2B products that need enterprise login features such as SAML single sign-on, SCIM provisioning and role based access control
problem: Enterprise customers demand SSO, provisioning, access control and audit logs before they buy, and building these features is slow and security sensitive for small software teams.
business_model: Open source auth infrastructure with a hosted paid tier, sold to developers building B2B SaaS
product_category: Developer tools, identity and access management

founders.name: Ulysse Carion
previous_startups: SSOReady (open source enterprise SSO toolkit, predecessor product)
founders.background_notes: YC page says he built Segment's permissions and identity resolution system and edited IETF RFC 8927. Education not listed.

founders.name: Ned O'Leary
previous_startups: SSOReady (open source enterprise SSO toolkit, predecessor product)
founders.background_notes: YC page lists no prior employers or education. Whether he co-built SSOReady is stated by the press only as a pair of founders.

technical_complexity.rationale: Standard identity protocols (SAML, SCIM, OIDC) are well documented but security critical and tedious, and the founders already built an SSO toolkit, so a small team could ship a first version.

defensibility.rationale: Open source code can be copied or self hosted by anyone, though auth becomes sticky once integrated into a customer's product.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Established auth vendors already served B2B SSO. Press in 2025 noted Twilio agreed to buy Stytch, closing November 2025, according to a vendor blog quoted in search results, so consolidation affected the space.

market_need_then: The YC launch post framed the product as open source auth for B2B SaaS, in the Auth0 mold but specific to B2B apps. Enterprise buyers routinely require SSO and provisioning, per the company's own product pitch.

identity.voice_and_tone: Security focused, security by default per the launch press release

branding.community_and_virality: Show HN thread in May 2025 and an open source GitHub repository; predecessor SSOReady had open source traction per press.

brand_strength.rationale: Little brand press beyond launch coverage; the name was changed from Okapi and no brand assets were found.

outcome_analysis: The directory marks Tesseral inactive, but no shutdown or sale was found and the company announced a 3.3 million dollar seed in May 2025, more than a year after the W24 batch. It looks like a slow build on open source credentials, with experienced identity founders. The inactive flag may be stale, so the outcome is unresolved.
notes: YC lists status Inactive but press shows activity in May 2025; conflict unresolved. Website fetch returned HTTP 402. Former name Okapi comes from a search summary of press coverage. No competitor source dated near the Winter 2024 batch was found (Show HN is May 2025), so the list is empty.
